verdict.rationale: Semgrep documents an official MCP server that a coding agent can connect to. Its marketing claims it can 'scan and fix AI-generated code the moment it's written', and a documented pre-commit hook can block issues at commit time, so the core path exists. However, the evidence never describes how the MCP server is wired into an agent's loop or that it gates code before it lands, so the coverage is incomplete. missing for 10: documentation of MCP server tools and setup for coding agents, evidence of agent-triggered pre-landing gating, independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent integration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can wire the scanner into my coding agent so AI-generated code is scanned for issues before it lands

citations.quote: official MCP server documented at https://docs.semgrep.dev/mcp
Scan and fix AI-generated code the moment it's written
The pre-commit framework can run semgrep when you commit changes. This is helpful in preventing secrets and security issues from leaking into your Git history.
